title: Shapes with a trait
description:
Use a trait so different shapes can be treated alike.

```
circle r=1.0: area 3.14
square 2.0: area 4.00
triangle 3,4,5: area 6.00
total: 13.14
```
hints: A default method has a body in the trait: `fn describe(&self) -> String { format!("{}: area {:.2}", self.name(), self.area()) }` (lesson 4.02).
`&dyn Shape` lets one slice hold different shapes; `&impl Shape` makes a separate copy of the function for each type.
requirements: `trait Shape { fn area(&self) -> f64; fn name(&self) -> String; fn describe(&self) -> String { ... } }` with a default `describe`.
`fn total_area(shapes: &[&dyn Shape]) -> f64` and a generic `fn print_one(s: &impl Shape)`.
stretch: Make a `Vec<Box<dyn Shape>>` and sort it by area.
